advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Write per-chunk progress so it survives an `os._exit` timeout (unbuffered stderr or a per-chunk subprocess `timeout=`), so a stall that hits the timeout still names its chunk
evidence: tests/conftest.py:48-54: the span is published via `warnings.warn(pytest.PytestWarning(...))`, which pytest records and forwards only after the test phase finishes
pyproject.toml:750-753: "because `timeout_method = \"thread\"` expires a test with `os._exit(1)` ... it kills the whole xdist worker (`node down: Not properly terminated`)"
tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py:80-89: each chunk calls `subprocess.run` with no per-call `timeout=`, so a stalled chunk blocks until pytest-timeout kills the process
tests/conftest.py:45: spans of 1 s or less are dropped silently, so in the log a fast chunk looks the same as a chunk that never ran
advisory.finding: The phase timings are lost in exactly the case this change is meant to diagnose. `_ci_timed_call` emits a span only in its `finally` after the call returns, and only as a pytest warning. With `timeout_method = "thread"`, pytest-timeout kills the worker with `os._exit(1)`. The finished phases' warnings are never forwarded, and the stalled chunk never reaches its `finally`. A Windows timeout therefore leaves no record of which chunk stalled or how long the earlier phases took.
scenarios: The next Windows sweep stalls in hash_object[k] and hits the per-test timeout. The worker is killed and no `[rebar-ci-timing]` line for any phase reaches the log. The diagnostic gives no answer.
advisory.suggested_fix: Before and after each chunk, write a line straight to `sys.__stderr__` with flush=True, e.g. `hash_object[k] start/done elapsed`, so it does not depend on pytest's warning capture. Alternatively, pass a per-chunk `timeout=` to `subprocess.run` that is well under the test budget, so a stall raises `TimeoutExpired` naming the chunk instead of being killed by `os._exit`.

tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py:78-79: `for k in range(_CHUNKS):\n        chunk = paths[k * len(paths) // _CHUNKS : (k + 1) * len(paths) // _CHUNKS]` — ten git processes now run instead of one
Commit message: "inside a single git hash-object --stdin-paths over 20,000 paths. Nothing says whether that is per-object NTFS cost or a stall between the stdin writer and git."
advisory.finding: The commit calls this "Measurement only", but it changes the workload being measured. One `git hash-object --stdin-paths` call over 20,000 paths, the invocation that hung, becomes ten separate git processes of about 2,000 paths each. A stall tied to the single large invocation (stdin size, one long-lived process holding the object DB) may not happen under the chunked fill. Then the sweep reports even, healthy chunks without having reproduced the condition.
scenarios: The hang depends on one git process consuming a 20,000-line stdin. After chunking it no longer reproduces, the timings look uniform, and the follow-up concludes from data that does not match the failing configuration.
